chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Sarah's new trio with Roy Haynes and Joe Benjamin
summary: With Crosby and Freeman gone, Haynes (a frustrated singer who knows every lyric) and Duke Ellington-associated bassist Joe Benjamin join; Haynes is his favorite accompanist drummer.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And then we came back to the United States, New York. When we came back, we had a few days rest, and it was time to hit the road again in the good old United States, and started hitting the clubs. But before we left New York, they had to get a trio together, which came up again. At that particular time, Israel Crosby I think was working with Benny Goodman, he'd gone on tour or something with Benny Goodman. Of course, Bruz had gone to California; I don't know what was happening. But we got Roy Haynes, the drummer Roy Haynes, and a bassist, Joe Benjamin, who was a New York fellow and had been associated with Duke Ellington's band for many years. He was an arranger, copyist, and he used to do a lot of the copying for Duke and Strayhorn.

Both are very fine musicians. Roy Haynes is a drummer that just turned out to be one of my favorite drummers that I have worked with. I think in a big band situation, Shadow Wilson was always my favorite, and of course, Art Blakey -- depending on the style that the band was playing. In a combo situation, and especially when it came to accompanying a singer, I think Roy Haynes is just about the greatest that I've ever worked with. First of all, we used to kid him a lot -- he's a frustrated singer himself. That's one of fhis
hidden talents. And he knows every song -- he knows the lyrics and everything. So when you're accompanying a singer, this can be invaluable.

Joe Benjamin, as I said before, was an excellent musician. He came from the school of George Duvivier and Milt Hinton, people that... There were his cronies. Bill Pemberton. And that's pretty good company to be in as a bassist.
